ovl-harthacnut-i|ovl-sigurd-snake-eye.claim: Harthacnut I of Denmark is the son of Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye and Blaeja of Northumbria.

hypotheses.label: Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye is his father
hypotheses.tradition: Ragnarssona þáttr / Ragnars saga Loðbrókar (13th-c. Icelandic tradition)
hypotheses.consequence: Carries the Danish royal line through Ragnar's son — the line to Gorm the Old and every Danish monarch after 1047.

hypotheses.label: A 'Sven' is his father (Sigurd's role uncertain)
hypotheses.consequence: The earliest near-contemporary source names Hardegon's father Sven — contradicting the þáttr by a century.

ovl-harthacnut-i|ovl-sigurd-snake-eye.contradictions: The þáttr is 13th-century; Adam of Bremen writes c. 1075, closer to the events but hostile to and distant from Danish court genealogy. Both cannot be simply true; neither is contemporary with Harthacnut (~916).
